Class I normally ī : ā : i : i. Snīðan changes ð to d in plural-based past forms and participle. Contracted wrēon has a special present and h/g stems.
Class II normally ēo or ū : ēa : u : o. Present2/3sg ēo→īe and ū→ȳ; Cook also allows ī for īe. cēosan s/r, sēoðan ð/d, and tēon h/g are lexical changes.

All those selected vowels are short. weorðan adds ð/d; winnan reduces nn; findan, bregdan and fēolan need explicit exception notes.

Dental d/t+ð gives tt (or t); d+st gives tst. s+st/ð gives st; ð before st may disappear and ð+ð may reduce. Geminates reduce before consonantal endings. g/h alternatives require the stated long-vowel/liquid environment; do not substitute h indiscriminately.

Cook permits full -est/-eð forms as well as syncopated cells. audited_inflection_rules.rule: Adjectivally used participles agree in gender, number and case, with the strong/weak choices already taught for adjectives. Present -ende follows the grēne-type strong declension; it is not a masculine agent noun in -end.

Cook61: present participles in the predicate as nominative/accusative are generally uninflected. Cook62: predicate past participles are generally indeclinable or take strong masculine endings. Cook179 allows uninflected predicate participles. Thus neuterplural dēor bunden is acceptable; dēor bundene is also licensed in verbal passive usage. Do not judge them by an obligatory attributive neuter-u rule.

Heavy-stem disyllabic participles can lose the unstressed vowel before vowel-initial inflections: bundenes→bundnes, bundenum→bundnum; hīeredes→hīerdes, hīeredum→hīerdum, hīerede→hīerde. Full vowels are often restored in West Saxon. Keep the full stem before -ne/-re/-ra; doubled n in bundenne is ordinary. Short-root fręmed/nęred and lufod retain their vowel in the selected model. Rare -u cells above are transparently paradigm-derived.

Weak participles are lexical principal parts, not a universal past-minus-e shortcut: hīerde→hīered, fręmede→fręmed, lufode→lufod, sealde→seald, worhte→worht, sętte→sętt, sęnde→sęnd, lǣdde→lǣd. Before inflection, syncope can bring a dental into contact with a voiceless stem and cause -t-, as Fulk113 scierped→scierpte. These audit examples do not newly assign unlisted verbs.

A past participle of an intransitive verb need not be passive. Source wæs geworden is a become/come-to-pass resultative closure, not a transitive passive. Auxiliary tense does not force one Modern English tense/aspect translation.

contracts.title: Complements and reported content
productive_outcomes: Use finite ðæt content clauses after selected knowing/saying frames, distinguishing factual indicative from contextual report subjunctive and bounded person/time reference.

Use hātan command and gesēon perception with an accusative actor and plain infinitive; distinguish naming and same-subject modal complements.
Use gewyrcean with an accusative object and an agreeing adjective; express bounded present unreal wishes with preterite subjunctives.
Use full new sunu, rīce and geðeahtend noun systems; complete selected nominal/adjectival forms within their lexical and number limits, with explicit familiar-class models and diagnostics.
Use seventeen complete present/preterite indicative systems, six command pairs and complete sēcan subjunctives with endings, stem changes and important exceptions.
Use explicitly assigned trade frames, dative benefit/usefulness, direct address, refusal, preference, accompaniment, temporal day, factual cause, partitive/appositional and bring-forth uses.
Complete all64 unchanged Cook II.9–12 prompts and33 original tasks; read the52word new dialogue independently and the62word exact source with its approved local support.
recognition_outcomes: Recognize stated noun number and adjective scope limits; singular manig and unassigned material/abstract count senses remain reference rather than production.
Recognize documented inflectional variants, including source sēceað, while distinguishing them from selected productive forms.
Interpret the exact source judgment/passive frames and unfamiliar forms through local helps without inferring whole impersonal, passive or participial systems.
bounded_scope: The actual eight active coverage contracts and cumulative registers are the sole prior-teaching authority. The archived course is evidence only; every Unit9 promotion retains its earlier supplied/recognition history.

Finite content clauses are productive after the selected knowing/saying frames only. Seeing receives the separately audited perception infinitive; no generalized seeing-content clause assignment is inferred.

Reported statements and dependent questions commonly select subjunctive in the stated settings. Contextual indicative can be valid; subjunctive does not assert falsity. Simultaneous present/past reports do not teach an automatic English backshift or the whole later tense/sequence system.
Inflected interrogative hwæðer and invariant whether hwæðer remain distinct lemmas and senses. Wh forms take their function's case inside the dependent clause.
Command hātan, perception gesēon and object-predicate gewyrcean each have a checked bounded lexical frame. Same-subject modal infinitives and naming hātan retain their distinct prior scopes.
The preterite subjunctive receives a bounded nonpast unreal-wish use. This does not teach general unreal conditionals or pluperfect constructions.

Only personal ēower in the assigned partitive frame is newly productive. Cook's hīe sume apposition is explained separately from a valid genitive alternative; other personal-genitive and indefinite systems remain limited.

The three new noun classes have literal complete NGDA tables. Other new nouns use complete earlier-class models plus explicit lexical stems and diagnostics. Every derivative cell is mapped, not falsely certified as printed verbatim.
Manig is productive as plural attributive many. Its singular forms and unassigned mass/abstract count-plurals remain recognition reference; displaying them creates no unassigned sense or syntax.

All17 selected new verb indicatives, six command pairs and sēcan subjunctives are complete. Other new infinitive citations remain supplied except the separately productive wician preference complement.
Sēceað is the exact source command variant, recognized with help. Sēcað is the selected productive plural command. Local fēt does not follow productively from prefixed āfēdan.

Supply the complete ivory, living-creatures and365-days phrases in their Cook tasks. The365 phrase is an explicit adaptation of numbered rules, not an exact source quotation or a complete higher-numeral system.

The source's seems frames, passives, among phrases, comparative furðra, substantival address and feeding phrase retain local support. Nominative hwilc/furðra must not be forced into the command/perception accusative-actor model.

All62 source words, four turns, thirteen notes and eleven help groups remain. The three conjectural is tokens and manuscript woruldcræftas note are explicit; nearby merchant/catalogue and smith passages remain unassigned.
Every public input and private required output is identified by actual form/sense IDs. Deliberately erroneous correction inputs are labeled and do not certify their syntax as good Old English.

The independent reviewer solves the actual learner tasks before reading any listed private answer/model file, freezes those solutions and discloses the earlier grammar-evidence role. Independent composition checks are not substitutes for the later full task/key review.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Sunu: N/A singular -u, G/D singular -a; N/G/A plural -a, D plural -um. The vowel is short. Cook records variation -u/-o outside genitives and dative plural, and later a-stem sunes/sunas. These are valid documented alternatives, not the selected target or an invitation to assign other u-stem lemmas.

Geðeahtend follows the masculine -end agent-noun pattern, not the inflecting present participle. Selected singular geðeahtend/-es/-e/zero; plural N/A geðeahtend, G geðeahtendra, D geðeahtendum. N/A plural -e and rarer -as are documented alternatives.

Rīce has singular rīce/rīces/rīce/rīce and plural rīcu/rīca/rīcum/rīcu. The lexical -e disappears before the case ending. Cook explicitly allows inserted i/e in the plural after c/g: rīciu/rīcia etc.; these are valid unselected variants.

Use explicit diagnostic stems: angel→angl-, fōdor→fōdr-, but ðyrel retains e. Cræft retains æ before its consonant cluster. Ealdormann follows mann in the final member: dat.sg and N/Apl ealdormęnn. Strong -e nouns replace final e before endings; -nes has -ness-. Smiððe/sīde are weak feminines; fyrspearca/trēowwyrhta/scēowyrhta/wyrhta/cęmpa weak masculines.

Behēfe is an -e adjective: replace lexical e with endings; selected strong feminine nominative singular and neuter N/A plural behēfu. Welig and manig retain medial i in the selected full paradigms and take -u in those cells (weligu/manigu). Wīs is heavy and lacks -u there. Wīsra adds comparative -r- without umlaut and declines weakly; genitive plural wīsra reduces doubled r beside s under Wright §259.3, as earlier lēofra does beside f. Strong feminine N/A plural -e is valid alongside selected -a; other variant cells require their own cited evidence rather than free analogical substitution. Manig is productive only as ordinary plural attributive many; its singular cells are recognition reference, without assigning many-a or substantival/partitive quantity constructions.

Mass/abstract unassigned plural senses remain outside independent production even though complete formal number paradigms are recorded. Hlæst wares and bęlg bellows are selected as plural; singular counterparts are recognition reference and do not add an unassigned singular sense. No source-supplied history is erased by a new production milestone.

audited_inflection_rules.statement: Each new verb has twelve explicit indicative cells, not just diagnostic principal parts. Present plurals share one form; preterite plurals share one form. Weak2sg past adds -st to the selected past1sg; strong2sg past takes the plural stem plus -e.

Cīepan takes -pte, āfēdan and selected weak rǣdan -dde; gestillan loses one l before -de; ālīehtan takes -hte with the two t sounds contracted. Bycgan/sēcan must learn bohte/sōhte. Fręmman retains doubled mm in most present forms but has fręmest/fręmeð and fręmede.

Select uncontracted present ālīehtest/ālīehteð to show the ending after the ht cluster. Present1sg ālīehte and past1/3sg ālīehte coincide; present2sg ālīehtest and past2sg ālīehtest coincide. No invented distinction from vowel length.

Rōwan changes ō→ē only in present2/3sg and has rēow past; blāwan ā→ǣ and blēow; bēatan ēa→īe and bēot; forlǣtan has forlēt; āstīgan has āstāg/āstige/āstigon. Final d/t + ð yields tt; g before st/ð yields h.
Prefixed begān follows gān throughout: begā/begǣst/begǣð/begāð; beēode/beēodest/beēodon. The prefix does not make the verb weak.
Wician, ðolian and gegaderian follow prior weakII: -ie/-ast/-að/-iað and -ode/-odest/-odon. Full new cells are displayed, though the class rules are prior.

Selected singular commands are rōw, byge, sēc, begā, gestil, rǣd; plural commands are the respective presentplural forms. Sēcan subjunctive uses sēce/sēcen and sōhte/sōhten. Source sēceað is preserved.

Full indicative display teaches indicative morphology only. Only six command pairs and the sēcan subjunctive are added. New citation infinitives are supplied except productive wician; source-only fēt, geðūht, gerǣd, tōgēiecte and libbende gesceafta remain locally supported. No systematic perfect, progressive, impersonal, infinitive tense or advanced sequence-of-tenses system follows.

Rǣdan is classified as usually weak in Cook§110 and explicitly as113 in his vocabulary: select rǣdde/rǣddon. Strong rēd/rēdon is a valid alternative system, not an independently required recall target.

Keep Cook hooked ę and macrons; selected bycgan/sēcan omit optional e before a vowel as Cook permits. BT bygeþ→bygeð is declared dental-letter normalization, with all quantities checked against Cook. Complete derived tables are new teaching material, not quoted historical paradigms.

recognition_outcomes: Recognize documented variants and reference-only number, adjective and instrumental cells without inferring productive syntax from their display.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Fæder is masculine; selected endingless genitive/dative singular fæder, with fæderes/fædere accepted; plural follows fæderas/fædera/fæderum/fæderas. Cook43.8 gives an exception to the strong masculine system, not an instruction to derive an umlaut dat singular.

Gāt: N/A singular gāt, selected G singular gāte (variant gǣt), D singular gǣt (variant gāte); N/A plural gǣt, G plural gāta, D plural gātum. The long vowel alternation is ā/ǣ; no -as plural or fictitious gǣtum.

Hand/woruld use strong feminine morphology with endingless accusative singular. Cook p297 explicitly directs hand to51.1.3; this lexical cross-reference licenses51.1 even though hand is absent from its exemplar list. Selected genitive/dative hande/worulde; source-authorized -a variants are accepted. A syncretic adjective ending alone does not disambiguate hand phrases.

Selected dryhten/dēofol/ęngel retain full nominative/accusative singular but use dryhtn-/dēofl-/ęngl- with endings; stem diagnostics control every cell. Compounds giesthūs and cweartern retain their terminal noun stems.

Apply complete prior strong/weak adjective systems. Retained-vowel disyllables, -e adjectives, long-stem unrihtwīs and double-consonant synfull have explicit diagnostics; swīðra has weak comparative morphology only. Displayed instrumental forms remain recognition unless the coordinator names an explicit productive means frame.

Hungry, sick, naked and unrighteous adjectives can name persons in the weak declension; the new people senses are separately assigned. Their case is governed by the containing clause, not by English the.

audited_inflection_rules.title: Selected weakI systems
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Present -e/-st/-ð/-að with selected contractions; past -e/-est/-e/-on added to the checked dental past stem. Long vowel+d gives dd in fēdde, scrȳdde, tōgelǣdde. Scęnc- takes -te, forwiern- -de.
audited_inflection_rules.variants: Cook permits tt/t contraction. BT explicitly attests fēt/fētt/fēdeð; selected production target fēt. Uncontracted and alternative spelling forms are not independently new recall targets.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Only declared indicative cells and separately listed complete command pairs; citations are supplied, not automatic infinitive production.

audited_inflection_rules.title: Selected weakII systems
audited_inflection_rules.rule: -ie, -ast, -að, plural -iað; preterite -ode, -odest, -ode, plural -odon. Command genēosa/genēosiað. Retain Cook longē in genēos-.
audited_inflection_rules.variants: Cook records plural -edon beside -odon, ig(e)/g beside i in endings, and alternate past vowels; -odon and i are the selected productive forms. Alternative weakI andswerian remains unassigned.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: No regular weakII rule licenses another verb’s lexical case frame.

audited_inflection_rules.title: Gewītan strongI
audited_inflection_rules.rule: ī present, ā first/third singular past, short i second singular/plural past; t-stem contractions yield gewītst/gewīt. Select gewāt/gewite/gewiton.
audited_inflection_rules.variants: Final tt beside t is source-rule supported; selected short t. Optional reflexive dative is attested, not obligatory in the chosen departure frame.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Do not confuse with gewitan know.

audited_inflection_rules.title: Supported unnan system
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Indicative ann/unnon; past ūðe/ūðest/ūðe/ūðon; subjunctive unne/unnen and ūðe/ūðen, all persons. Present indicative2sg visibly has no assigned form. Direct addressed command uses second-person unne/unnen.
audited_inflection_rules.variants: Cook an(n) permits an and ann; selected ann. Cook labels unne imperative; Fulk describes subjunctive substitution. Both source descriptions are preserved.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: No invented anst/unnest/unne indicative2sg or unnað formal imperative. The omission records checked-source limits, not universal nonattestation.

audited_inflection_rules.title: Two bounded experiencer systems
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Hyngreð/hyngrede with accusative experiencer and no expressed nominative; ðyncð/ðūhte with dative experiencer and a singular neuter nominative stimulus. Each defined finite system has exactly present3sg and past3sg.
audited_inflection_rules.variants: Other personal and case frames are documented but not assigned; source quantity/spelling is explicit.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: No fabricated personal paradigm for the subjectless frame; no promotion of Unit9 entire passive/judgment construction.

audited_inflection_rules.title: Case form and contextual role
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Se has masculine/neuter singular ðȳ (variant ðon); strong gōd has gōde in those cells. Nouns, feminine singular and plural express this relation with dative-shaped forms. The food noun retains mete-dat-sg canonical identity; context marks instrumental function.
audited_inflection_rules.variants: Prose mid+DAT ordinary; bare means more characteristic of poetry. Do not assign Anglian mid+distinct instrumental as the normal EWS production choice.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: All six newly promoted distinct cells are displayed; earlier ðes/hwā instruments remain recognition-only.

audited_inflection_rules.description: Complete NGDA noun patterns use the cited Cook class models with each lexical stem. Mass/abstract plural reference cells do not establish new count senses.

Bæð keeps æ in singular and has a in plural baðu/baða/baðum; geat keeps ea in singular and has a in plural gatu/gata/gatum; sīðfæt has sīðfatas/sīðfata/sīðfatum. The changes belong to these checked lexemes, not all written vowels.
Seolh loses h and lengthens eo before case endings: sēol-. Bare nominative/accusative singular retain seolh. This completes a newly used subpattern.
Selected seolfor/frōfor/ceaster/winter use seolfr-/frōfr-/ceastr-/wintr- before endings. Īsern retains its medial e because the second syllable ends in rn; sumer retains its medial vowel.

Sumer and winter retain complete ordinary masculine systems; Cook43.5 also records occasional genitive/dative singular and nominative plural -a. The variants are accepted, not separately tested recall.

All ordinary adjective NGDA cells are productive; distinct instrumental masculine/neuter singular cells remain recognition reference. Blæc changes æ to a before vowel endings; consonantal endings retain æ. The weak genitive plural likewise retains æ before the shared strong ending -ra: blæcra in every gender. Stille/smylte retain final e only where no ending replaces it. Stille simplifies ll before consonantal endings: stilne/stilre/stilra, but stille/stilles/stillum.

The selected complete fæger, gesyndig and ðurstig tables retain the medial vowel. Cook57.3 also licenses syncope and occasional endingless feminine singular/neuter plural; the exact source gesyndge remains a separately supported syncopated realization. Fæger has independently attested retained and syncopated forms.

Dēorwierðra and fægerra are weak throughout, including predicates. Remove final e of dēorwierðe before -ra. Fægerra/fægerre are directly documented by BT264a. Genitive plurals dēorwierðra/fægerra apply the already taught consonant reduction; these full paradigms are rule-derived, not verbatim source tables.
